artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan fixing three channel-confusion defects in the orchestrate cycle-plan pipeline: structural fd-3 stdout/JSON discipline, charge-free replay of unconsumed plan compositions, and truthful Class C/D predispatch-review negatives, plus a maintained lint for the defect class.

memory_candidates.content: Shell-pipeline bug class: a channel carrying two meanings. A script whose stdout is a machine-readable payload (JSON/NDJSON) leaks prose into it whenever any callee prints to stdout; per-call-site `>&2` fixes are stopgaps that must be re-applied at every future call site. The structural remedy is `exec 3>&1 1>&2` at script entry with the payload emitted to fd 3 — fd 1 and 2 both become diagnostics, so no future callee can contaminate the data channel. This has an exact mirror image on the ingest side: capturing a collaborator with `2>&1` folds its stderr into the payload being parsed. The NDJSON `while read` shape is the dangerous half, because the collaborator still exits 0, the degraded-path warning never fires, and a garbage row is ingested while success is reported. The two directions need independent fixes (fd-3 governs what a script emits; a stdout-only capture helper governs what it ingests), and a detector for the class must cover jq-pipe, jq here-string, AND while-read consumption or it silently misses the worst case.
